{{ElectionsCT}}
The '''2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Connecticut''' will be held on Tuesday, November 6, 2018, to elect the five [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representatives]] from the state of [[Connecticut]], one from each of the state's five congressional districts. The elections will coincide with the [[Connecticut gubernatorial election, 2018|gubernatorial election]], as well as [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2018|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[United States Senate elections, 2018|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[United States elections, 2018#State elections|state]] and [[United States elections, 2018#Local elections|local elections]].

{{Toclimit|limit=2}}

==District 1==
{{seealso|Connecticut's 1st congressional district}}
The 1st district is located in the north-central part of the state, and is anchored by the state capital of [[Hartford, Connecticut|Hartford]]. It includes parts of [[Hartford County, Connecticut|Hartford]], [[Litchfield County, Connecticut|Litchfield]], and [[Middlesex County, Connecticut|Middlesex]] counties. The incumbent is Democrat [[John B. Larson|John Larson]], who has represented the district since 1999. He was re-elected to a tenth term with 64% of the vote in 2016.

===Democratic primary===
* [[John B. Larson|John Larson]], incumbent<ref>http://docquery.fec.gov/pdf/167/201704309053487167/201704309053487167.pdf</ref>

==District 2==
{{seealso|Connecticut's 2nd congressional district}}
The 2nd district is located in the eastern part of the state, and includes all of [[New London County, Connecticut|New London]], [[Tolland County, Connecticut|Tolland]], and [[Windham County, Connecticut|Windham]] counties and parts of [[Hartford County, Connecticut|Hartford]], [[Middlesex County, Connecticut|Middlesex]], and [[New Haven County, Connecticut|New Haven]] counties. The incumbent is Democrat [[Joe Courtney (politician)|Joe Courtney]], who has represented the district since 2007. He was re-elected to a sixth term with 63% of the vote in 2016. The [[National Republican Congressional Committee]] has outlined this district as one of the 36 Democratic-held districts it is targeting in 2018.<ref>https://www.nrcc.org/2017/02/08/nrcc-announces-initial-offensive-targets-2018-cycle/</ref>

* [[Joe Courtney (politician)|Joe Courtney]], incumbent<ref>http://docquery.fec.gov/pdf/628/201701099041203628/201701099041203628.pdf</ref>

==District 3==
{{seealso|Connecticut's 3rd congressional district}}
The 3rd district is located in the central part of the state and contains the city of [[New Haven, Connecticut|New Haven]] and its surrounding suburbs. It includes parts of [[Fairfield County, Connecticut|Fairfield]], [[Middlesex County, Connecticut|Middlesex]], and [[New Haven County, Connecticut|New Haven]] counties. The incumbent is Democrat [[Rosa DeLauro]], who has represented the district since 1991. She was re-elected to a fourteenth term with 69% of the vote in 2016.

===Democratic primary===
* [[Rosa DeLauro]], incumbent<ref>http://docquery.fec.gov/pdf/841/201612219040804841/201612219040804841.pdf</ref>

===Republican primary===

==District 4==
{{seealso|Connecticut's 4th congressional district}}
The 4th district is located in the southwestern part of the state, extending from [[Bridgeport, Connecticut|Bridgeport]], the largest city in the state, to [[Greenwich, Connecticut|Greenwich]]. It includes parts of [[Fairfield County, Connecticut|Fairfield]] and [[New Haven County, Connecticut|New Haven]] counties. The incumbent is Democrat [[Jim Himes]], who has represented the district since 2009. He was re-elected to a fifth term with 60% of the vote in 2016.

===Democratic primary===
* [[Jim Himes]], incumbent<ref>http://docquery.fec.gov/pdf/799/201612289040903799/201612289040903799.pdf</ref>

==District 5==
{{seealso|Connecticut's 5th congressional district}}
The 5th district is located in the northwestern part of the state and includes parts of [[Fairfield County, Connecticut|Fairfield]], [[Hartford County, Connecticut|Hartford]], [[Litchfield County, Connecticut|Litchfield]], and [[New Haven County, Connecticut|New Haven]] counties. The incumbent is Democrat [[Elizabeth Esty]], who has represented the district since 2013. She was re-elected to a third term with 58% of the vote in 2016. Esty is not running for reelection in 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last=Connolly |first=Griffin |date=April 3, 2018 |title=Rep. Elizabeth Esty Won't Seek Re-election in Wake of Abusive Staffer Disclosures |url=https://www.rollcall.com/news/politics/rep-elizabeth-esty-wont-seek-re-election-wake-abusive-staffer-disclosures |work=[[Roll Call]] |location=Washington, DC |access-date=April 3, 2018 }}</ref>

===Democratic primary===
'''Declared'''
*Mary Glassman, former [[First Selectman]] of [[Simsbury, Connecticut|Simsbury]], and candidate for Lieutenant Governor in 2006 and 2010<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ctmirror.org/2018/04/02/mary-glassman-jumps-suddenly-open-5th-cd-race|title=Mary Glassman jumps into suddenly open 5th District race - The CT MirrorThe CT Mirror|website=ctmirror.org|language=en-US|accessdate=2018-04-03}}</ref>
*[[Jahana Hayes]], 2016 [[National Teacher of the Year]]<ref>https://ctmirror.org/2018/05/17/jahana-hayes-art-linares-run-primaries</ref>

'''Declined'''
*[[Elizabeth Esty]], incumbent congresswoman<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/powerpost/esty-calls-for-ethics-review-of-her-handling-of-baker-allegations-dismissal/2018/04/02/7ed2cc14-3685-11e8-9c0a-85d477d9a226_story.html|title=Elizabeth Esty won’t seek reelection amid scrutiny of chief of staff’s departure|last=Viebeck|first=Elise|date=2018-04-02|work=Washington Post|accessdate=2018-04-03|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}}</ref>
*Liz Linehan, state representative<ref name=":0">{{cite news|url=http://www.ctnewsjunkie.com/archives/entry/20180402_race_for_5th_cd_opens_up|title=Race for 5th CD Opens Up {{!}} CT News Junkie|work=CT News Junkie|access-date=2018-04-03|language=en}}</ref>
